title: Console fallback skeleton: lightweight dashboard routes and tracing-sampler acceptance
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Propose a 'Fallback Skeleton' pattern for the Console MVP that provides a lightweight, dependable route for dashboards and a tracing-sampler mechanism to reduce telemetry cost and surface the most actionable signals. Goal is to ship a minimal, high-confidence surface that preserves alertability and high-impact troubleshooting while removing expensive visualizations and heavy query paths that risk missing the launch window.

Scope decisions / cuts: 
- INCLUDE: a single compact route per major product area (Routes -> Summary card, Top errors, Cost delta), route-level aggregated cost breakdown (3 buckets), and a tracing sampler that captures 1) a deterministic small-sample for cold-starts and 2) probabilistic sampling for steady-state.
- EXCLUDE (deferred): expanded multi-card dashboards, per-token cost heatmaps, CSV export, rich drilldowns, ad-hoc query builder, and full-fidelity per-request trace capture.
- Observability tradeoff: prioritize SLO-safe latency and storage costs over absolute completeness of traces; provide a sampled representative set for postmortem and SLI correlation.

Rationale: Current full-surface telemetry and per-request capture will add storage, query cost, and end-to-end latency. By shipping a fallback skeleton with strict card budget and sampling strategy we unblock GA while keeping a clear roadmap to restore advanced features post-launch.

Acceptance gating & rollout: Feature-flagged rollout to 10% customers -> 50% -> 100%, and gated on trace-sample quality and route latency SLO during each expansion window.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The fallback route renders within 250ms P95 for non-empty cached requests and within 450ms cold for first-time views in the EU region.
AC-2: Dashboard payload contains at most 3 visible cards on initial render (Summary, Top Errors, Cost Delta) and supports a single secondary action to 'Inspect sample traces'.
AC-3: Tracing sampler reduces stored traces by >=75% vs full-capture baseline while retaining 95% of unique error signatures (measured by hash) over a 24h window.

AC-4: Route-level cost breakdown shows top-3 contributors with estimated token-cost deltas; values must be within +/- 10% of the costly-analytics baseline for representative workloads (internal benchmark suite).

AC-5: Rollout gating requires no more than 1 critical production incident attributable to the new route per 14 days during staged rollout, otherwise automatic rollback to previous feature flag state occurs.
AC-6: QA checklist complete: smoke tests, load test at 3x expected peak for the route, and UX sanity pass by design (Figma link reviewed).
AC-7: Console exposes a single admin toggle for the tracing sampler rate and a runtime metric for sampled vs dropped traces visible in the Debug dashboard.
AC-8: Documentation: PRD, quickstart, and release notes published to Confluence and linked in the ticket before GA.
AC-9: No security or compliance blockers remain; any KMS/HSM integration deferred is documented with mitigations for customer data residency.
AC-10: Telemetry: Compare pre/post rollout dashboards for CPU/DB storage cost and ensure aggregate telemetry cost does not exceed modeled budget (<= +15% of baseline for the combined service).
notes:
Design anchor: compact cards aim to surface deterministic actionable items. Tracing sampler design: deterministic capture of first N requests per route per pod (N=5) + probabilistic steady-state (p=0.02) with adaptive burst allowance on detected error spikes. Sampling parameters are tunable via admin UI and runtime flags.

Implementation sketch: ENG to build a lightweight route backed by reduced telemetry queries (pre-aggregates), DEVOPS to add sampling middleware to ingestion pipeline, and DX to author a short help guide.

Deferred work (post-GA): reintroduce per-request trace capture for paid tiers, enrich drilldowns, add export & custom filters, interactive token heatmap.
